q: Task: install the Traefik chart from /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz as release traefik into namespace ingress (the namespace does not exist), with deployment.replicas=2. Which command is correct?
options: helm install traefik /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz -n ingress --create-namespace --set deployment.replicas=2
helm install /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz traefik -n ingress --set deployment.replicas=2
helm upgrade traefik /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz -n ingress --set deployment.replicas=2
helm template traefik /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz -n ingress --create-namespace --set deployment.replicas=2
explain: helm install takes the release name first and then the chart, and --create-namespace creates the missing namespace. The reversed argument order is wrong, upgrade without --install fails because the release does not exist, and template installs nothing.

q: Release web was installed with `--set image.tag=1.28 --set replicaCount=3`. A colleague runs `helm upgrade web ./web-chart --set replicaCount=5`. What happens to image.tag?
options: It stays 1.28, because Helm always remembers previous values
It goes back to the default value from the chart's values.yaml
The upgrade fails because image.tag is missing
It stays 1.28 only if the release was installed with --atomic
explain: Without --reuse-values (or -f with all values) an upgrade computes values from the chart defaults plus whatever is given in that command. --atomic (--rollback-on-failure in Helm 4) has nothing to do with values.

q: `helm history api -n prod` shows revisions 1 (superseded), 2 (superseded), 3 (deployed). You run `helm rollback api 1 -n prod`. What does the history show afterwards?
options: Revisions 2 and 3 are deleted, revision 1 is deployed
Revision 1 is deployed, revisions 2 and 3 are superseded
A new revision 4 with the content of revision 1 is deployed
Revision 3 stays deployed until helm upgrade is run
explain: A rollback creates a new revision with the configuration of the requested revision; history is neither deleted nor changed. That is why after a rollback you can return to the state of revision 3 again.

q: You installed release monitoring into namespace observability. `helm list` returns an empty list. What is the most likely reason?
options: The release was installed with --wait so it has not finished yet
Helm 4 stores the release in a ConfigMap that helm list does not read
The release was installed using helm template
helm list looks only at the current namespace; you need helm list -n observability or -A
explain: Helm works in the namespace from the context if -n is not given, so a release in another namespace is not visible. Helm stores state in Secrets, and helm install is not the same as helm template.

q: A task asks you to save the manifests that chart /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz would create (with service.spec.type=NodePort) to /root/traefik.yaml, without installing. Which command?
options: helm template traefik /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz --set service.spec.type=NodePort > /root/traefik.yaml
helm show values /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz --set service.spec.type=NodePort > /root/traefik.yaml
helm get manifest traefik > /root/traefik.yaml
helm pull /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz --untar -d /root/traefik.yaml
explain: helm template renders manifests locally with the given values. show values prints only the chart's values.yaml, get manifest requires an existing release, and pull only unpacks the chart.

q: You have a Helm 3 script with `helm upgrade --install app ./chart --atomic --force`. What happens in Helm 4?
options: The command fails because both flags were removed
The command works, but with warnings; the new names are --rollback-on-failure and --force-replace
The command works without warnings; the flags are unchanged
--atomic works, and --force was renamed to --server-side
explain: Helm 4 renamed --atomic to --rollback-on-failure and --force to --force-replace; the old names still work with a deprecation warning. --server-side is a separate flag for the apply method.

q: Which TWO commands show the correct chart value names before installation, so you do not have to guess keys? (Choose TWO.)
options: helm show values traefik/traefik
helm get values traefik -n traefik
helm show values /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz
helm status traefik -n traefik
helm history traefik -n traefik
explain: helm show values works with both repo/chart and a local .tgz and does not require a release. get values, status and history work only on an already installed release.

q: The overlays/prod directory has a kustomization.yaml with resources: [../../base] and images: [{name: nginx, newTag: "1.28"}]. You run `kubectl apply -f overlays/prod/`. What happens?
options: The base is applied with image tag 1.28
kubectl recognizes kustomization.yaml and behaves like apply -k
Only the base is applied without changes
kubectl tries to apply kustomization.yaml as a regular manifest and reports an error, and the overlay is not applied
explain: -f reads the YAML files in the directory as regular manifests; a Kustomization is not an API object, so apply fails. Kustomize needs kubectl apply -k overlays/prod.

q: After adding `commonLabels: {team: payments}` to kustomization.yaml and running `kubectl apply -k .` over an existing Deployment, you get the error: spec.selector: Invalid value ... field is immutable. How do you add the label without this error?
options: Use labels with pairs: {team: payments} and includeSelectors: false
Add namePrefix: payments-
Run kubectl apply -k . --force
Move the label into configMapGenerator
explain: commonLabels always adds labels to selectors too, and a Deployment selector is immutable. The labels field without includeSelectors changes only metadata labels. namePrefix would create a new Deployment, and a generator does not add labels to objects.

q: An overlay contains a configMapGenerator for app-config. When you change the literal LOG_LEVEL=debug and run apply -k again, what happens?
options: ConfigMap app-config is updated, and Pods do not see the change until a manual restart
A ConfigMap with a new hash suffix is created, the Deployment gets the new reference and does a rolling update
apply fails because a ConfigMap with a generated name cannot be changed
Kustomize deletes the old Deployment and creates a new one
explain: The generator adds a content hash to the name and updates references, so a content change changes the Pod template and triggers a rollout. Without the hash (disableNameSuffixHash) the behavior would be as in the first option.

q:
What is missing from this entry in kustomization.yaml?

patches:
- patch: |-
    - op: replace
      path: /spec/replicas
      value: 5
options: A path field with the file name
apiVersion and kind in the patch itself
target (e.g. kind: Deployment, name: web), because a JSON 6902 patch always requires a target
The field options.allowNameChange: true
explain: A JSON 6902 patch is a list of operations without any object identification, so Kustomize must know which resource it applies to. apiVersion/kind are given in a strategic merge patch, and allowNameChange is for renaming.

q: You apply a CRD with metadata.name: backup.kurs.local, spec.group: kurs.local, names.plural: backups. The API server rejects it. Why?
options: The group must contain at least two dots
scope is not specified and it has no default value of Namespaced
kind must be identical to the plural
metadata.name must be <plural>.<group>, i.e. backups.kurs.local
explain: The CRD name must match names.plural and spec.group. The group only needs a dot, and kind is the CamelCase singular (Backup).

q: You try `kubectl apply -f backup.yaml` (kind: Backup, apiVersion: kurs.local/v1) and get: no matches for kind "Backup" in version "kurs.local/v1". What do you check first?
options: kubectl get crd | grep kurs.local and whether the CRD serves version v1
Whether a RoleBinding exists for the user
The kube-scheduler logs
Whether the operator Pod is running
explain: The message means the API server does not know that kind in that version: the CRD is not installed, not Established, or the version does not have served: true. RBAC would give forbidden, and the operator does not affect whether a CR can be created.

q: The backup-operator is running, but new Backup objects never get a status. The operator logs show: backups.kurs.local "db-nightly" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:backup-system:backup-operator" cannot update resource "backups/status". What is the fix?
options: Add the update verb on the backups resource to the ClusterRole
Add the backups/status subresource with the update and patch verbs to the operator's ClusterRole
Change the CRD scope to Cluster
Set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the operator
explain: Status is written through the separate /status subresource, which requires its own rule. Permission on backups does not cover backups/status, and the CRD scope and token are not the cause.

q: What happens when you run `kubectl delete crd backups.kurs.local` in a cluster that has 40 Backup objects?
options: The deletion fails while Backup objects exist
The CRD is deleted, the Backup objects stay in etcd and come back when the CRD is recreated
The CRD and all Backup objects are deleted
Only objects in the default namespace are deleted
explain: Deleting a CRD removes the API endpoint and all custom resources of that type; a recreated CRD is empty. That is why Helm does not delete CRDs on uninstall.

q: Task: write the documentation of all spec fields of the Backup resource to /root/backup-spec.txt (the backups.kurs.local CRD has an openAPIV3Schema with descriptions). Fastest solution?
options: kubectl get crd backups.kurs.local -o yaml > /root/backup-spec.txt
kubectl describe backups > /root/backup-spec.txt
kubectl api-resources --api-group=kurs.local > /root/backup-spec.txt
kubectl explain backup.spec --recursive > /root/backup-spec.txt
explain: kubectl explain reads the OpenAPI schema the CRD publishes and prints the fields with descriptions. get crd gives the whole CRD YAML, describe describes existing objects, and api-resources only lists types.

q: A CRD has a schema with spec.properties: schedule (string) and target (string). You apply a CR with an extra field spec.retentionDays: 7. What happens (kubectl v1.35, default strict validation)?
options: kubectl reports an error about the unknown field spec.retentionDays
The field is silently stored in etcd
The operator automatically extends the CRD schema
The API server adds the field to the schema as a string
explain: kubectl sends strict field validation by default, so an unknown field not in the schema causes an error; with weaker validation the field would be dropped (pruning), not stored. The schema changes only by editing the CRD.

q: Put the steps for upgrading Helm release ingress to a new chart while keeping existing values, with verification and the option to roll back, in order.
options: helm upgrade ingress /opt/kurs/charts/traefik-*.tgz -n ingress --reuse-values
helm history ingress -n ingress
helm get values ingress -n ingress
helm rollback ingress -n ingress (if the new revision does not work)
kubectl get pods -n ingress
explain: First you look at the current values, then upgrade with --reuse-values, check the Pods, see the new revision in history and roll back to the previous one if needed.

q: Match each CRD field with its purpose.
options: spec.scope
versions[].storage
versions[].schema.openAPIV3Schema
names.shortNames
versions[].additionalPrinterColumns
targets: Extra columns in kubectl get output
Validation and pruning of custom resource fields
A short name for kubectl (e.g. bk)
The version in which objects are stored in etcd (exactly one)
explain: scope determines whether CRs are namespaced, storage marks the version for etcd, openAPIV3Schema validates fields, shortNames give an alias, and additionalPrinterColumns add columns. A CRD has no field for controller replicas.

q: Match each Kustomize field with its effect.
options: namePrefix: prod-
images: [{name: nginx, newTag: "1.28"}]
secretGenerator
resources: [../../base]
targets: Includes the manifests from the base kustomization
Creates a Secret with a hash suffix in its name
Changes the tag of all containers using the nginx image
Adds a prefix to object names and updates references
explain: namePrefix changes names and references, images changes the image tag, secretGenerator creates a Secret with a hash, and resources pulls in the base. Selectors are changed by commonLabels or labels with includeSelectors.
